No sell-side note, article or transcript question has laid out the implied Q4 step-down - the Q3 call transcript records that no analyst pressed management on it and management declined to forecast Q4. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be drifting -5.96% over 20 days into the print at exactly the $10 average analyst target; it would be marked up toward the $13 KeyBanc target set 2026-08-21.

evidence.text: Colorado - InnovAge's home and largest state - enacted roughly $270M of Medicaid reimbursement cuts for FY2026-27, taking most fee-for-service rates down to 85% of Medicare from 2026-04-01 and layering a further 2.0% across-the-board reduction on HCBS waiver services for dates of service from 2026-07-01, published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors; PACE Medicaid capitation is set beneath an upper payment limit derived from exactly those FFS/HCBS costs, so the FY2027 Colorado rate InnovAge must build its first FY2027 guide around is flat-to-down rather than the mid-single-digit increases of prior years.
evidence.why_not_priced: The qualitative warning IS on the wire - the CFO said on 2026-05-06 that FY2027 Medicaid increases 'may be lower than what we have experienced historically' and the CEO guided Medicare to +1.5-2%. What is not on the wire is the mechanism or the size: no published note quantifies the 85%-of-Medicare reset or the 2% July-1 HCBS cut, and the July-1 piece was only confirmed in a state provider bulletin issued a month after InnovAge's last communication. If this were priced you would see a published FY2027 EBITDA estimate cut or a downgrade in the four months since the Q3 call; instead the only rated action on file is KeyBanc reiterating Buy with a $13 target on 2026-08-21 and the stock sits at the $10 average target.
evidence.independence: Independently corroborated by state budget reporting: https://www.cpr.org/2026/04/01/colorado-budget-draft-billion-shortfall-2026/ (2026-04-01, on the ~$1.5bn shortfall and the Medicaid-led cuts) and https://www.vaildaily.com/news/colorado-new-budget-cuts-medicaid/ on the signed budget. evidence.text: The US$10m buyback that drove the stock +21.5% on 2026-09-03 and anchored the +76% five-session run is 17 Education's sixth consecutive annual US$10m authorisation (Nov 2021, Sep 2022, Sep 2023, Sep 2024, Sep 2025, Sep 2026) and is a straight rollover of the identical US$10m program that ran 2025-09-04 to 2026-09-04 and expired four days before this one started.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 2026-09-03 release makes no reference to any prior program, and the identical predecessor was buried inside the 2025-09-04 Q2 earnings 6-K rather than issued as its own headline. Volume on 2026-09-03 was 2,789,500 ADS against a 20-day median of 4,600 before the event - a ~600x spike in a 10.86m-ADS name with no sell-side coverage and no option chain. If the market had recognised this as an expiring-program rollover rather than new capital, the tape would show a low-volume drift, not a 600x-volume +21.5% day followed by three more up sessions on no news at all; and the stock would not still be adding +18% intraday on 2026-09-08 on roughly average volume with nothing in the wire since 2026-09-03.

evidence.text: Q1 2026's headline RMB99.5m revenue (+359% YoY) was drawn largely out of a one-off pre-sale balance rather than new demand: deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 to RMB104.5m at 2026-03-31, a RMB61.5m drawdown equal to 62% of the quarter's revenue, and cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB406.9m to RMB352.3m) against a reported net loss of only RMB19.4m - 2.8x the loss.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no sell-side model on a US$37.4m-market-cap name, no consensus estimate published, and every piece of wire copy on the quarter carried only the two lines the company led with - '+359.0% year-over-year' and 'Yiqi Aixue revenue more than quadrupled'. The Q1 earnings call had no Q&A at all (the operator recorded no questions), so the drawdown was never put to management. Had the market modelled the unwind, a stock at 0.73x its own liquid assets would not need a recurring buyback authorisation to re-rate 76%; the re-rating is being justified by the growth narrative, which is precisely the thing the deferred-revenue line qualifies. The remaining RMB104.5m balance also caps how much of this can repeat.
evidence.independence: The year-ago control comes from a DIFFERENT filing and shows the drawdown is not seasonal: in Q1 2025 deferred revenue fell only RMB40.4m to RMB36.9m, i.e. RMB3.5m or 16% of that quarter's RMB21.7m revenue, versus 62% this year, and cash plus deposits fell RMB25.9m against a LARGER net loss of RMB30.9m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025084635/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-06-11). The Q4/FY2025 release shows where the balance came from - RMB40.4m at 2024-12-31 and RMB36.5m at 2025-09-30 building to RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 on pre-sales of the new consumer product: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526122709/yq-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-25) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312525313418/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-12-10). NOTE: the RMB61.5m deferred-revenue drawdown and the RMB54.6m cash decline are two readings of the same Q1 2026 document and are filed here as one finding, not two.

evidence.text: The company dismissed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu as its auditor effective 2026-05-27 and appointed Marcum Asia CPAs LLP for the year ending 2026-12-31 - i.e. it dropped a Big Four auditor two quarters after its revenue recognition profile changed beyond recognition, and the Q2 2026 numbers about to be released are the first reported under the new firm.

Deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 31-Dec-2025 to RMB104.5m at 31-Mar-2026, so RMB61.4m of the RMB99.5m of Q1 revenue that produced the headline '+359% YoY' was a drawdown of Q4 2025 pre-sale orders: implied new billings were only about RMB38m, less than the RMB43.2m spent on sales and marketing in the same quarter, and cash plus restricted cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB407.0m to RMB352.4m) against a reported net loss of just RMB19.4m.
evidence.why_not_priced: The wire copy on this quarter is 'AI learning app lifts 17EdTech revenue 359%, net loss down 37.4%' — headline growth and headline loss. The deferred-revenue line sits in the condensed balance sheet at the back of the same release and nobody has subtracted it: no sell-side analyst publishes an estimate on YQ, stockanalysis.com's news feed carries only the three headline items, and the release contains no cash-flow statement so the RMB54.6m cash decline versus a RMB19.4m loss has to be computed by differencing two balance sheets. If this were priced, the stock would not have closed the entire discount to book — shareholders' equity of RMB269.1m (US$39.0m) at 31-Mar-2026 against a US$37.5m market cap at $3.45 puts YQ at roughly 1.0x a book value that is falling about RMB18m a quarter, i.e. the deep-value cushion that justified the whole run has already gone. With only RMB104.5m of deferred balance left, the Q2 release's own deferred-revenue and cash lines are where this becomes visible for a second consecutive quarter.
evidence.independence: Chinese trade coverage independently describes the Q4 2025 launch as a membership product sold on pre-orders ('achieved strong pre-sale orders'), which is the mechanism: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526122709/yq-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-25). Separately, Tencent News coverage of 2026-07-12 attributes the growth to a To-B/To-G 'smart paper-pen + AI' school solution covering 2,000+ schools rather than to the consumer app the English release credits, which is a second, unrelated reason to doubt the revenue narrative: https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260712A066GD00. evidence.text: There is a real structural bid under the stock that cuts against the fade: the CEO's 10b5-1 plan runs to 31-Mar-2028 and the US$10m authorisation is live, against a non-Liu share base of only about 6.4m ADS-equivalent (542.2m shares outstanding less Andy Chang Liu's 223.9m / 41.30%) and a pre-spike median volume of 4,600 ADSs a day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The float arithmetic requires combining the 13D/A percentages with the 20-F share count, and no aggregator does it: stockanalysis.com reports 10.86m shares outstanding and a US$37.45m market cap with no float adjustment at all. A stock where 41.3% is held by one person and baseline turnover is 4,600 ADSs a day cannot absorb even partial execution of a US$10m programme without gapping, so the downside from the four negative findings above is genuinely dampened relative to what the fundamentals alone would imply — which is why my net number is -9.5 and not the -11.5 the negatives sum to.
